question_text: 1. Calculate the capacitance of a parallel-plate single-layer capacitor made using a $\mathrm{BaTiO}_{3}$ formulation of $k=2000$. Assume $d=3 \mathrm{~mm}$ and $A=5 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$. What is the volumetric efficiency of this capacitor? 2. Calculate the capacitance of an MLC comprised of 60 dielectric layers connected in parallel using $N=61$ electrodes. The thickness of each layer is 50 $\mu \mathrm{m}$. The cross-sectional area of this capacitor is also $5 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$, and $k=2000$. What is the volumetric efficiency of this capacitor? 3. What is the ratio of the volumetric efficiencies for multilayer and single-layer capacitors? Give your answer as a tuple (volumetric efficiency in 1, volumetric efficiency in 2, ratio of volumetric efficiencies).The units of each required answer are (nF/mm^3, nF/mm^3, ), respectively.
response:
## Solution

### Part 1: Single-layer capacitor

$$C_1 = \frac{k\varepsilon_0 A}{d} = \frac{2000 \times 8.854\times10^{-12} \times 5\times10^{-6}}{3\times10^{-3}} = 29.51\text{ pF}$$

Volume $V_1 = A\cdot d = 5\times 3 = 15\text{ mm}^3$.

Volumetric efficiency $= C_1/V_1 = 0.02951/15 \approx 0.00197\text{ nF/mm}^3$.

Note the simplification: $\dfrac{C}{V} = \dfrac{k\varepsilon_0 A/d}{A\cdot d} = \dfrac{k\varepsilon_0}{d^2}$.

### Part 2: Multilayer capacitor (60 layers in parallel, N=61 electrodes)

Each layer: $C_{\text{layer}} = \dfrac{k\varepsilon_0 A}{d_{\text{layer}}}$ with $d_{\text{layer}}=50\,\mu\text{m}$.

Total $C_2 = 60\,C_{\text{layer}} = 106.25\text{ nF}$.

Total thickness $= 60\times 50\,\mu\text{m} = 3\text{ mm}$, so $V_2 = 5\times 3 = 15\text{ mm}^3$ (same volume!).

Volumetric efficiency $= C_2/V_2 = \dfrac{k\varepsilon_0}{d_{\text{layer}}^2} \approx 7.0832\text{ nF/mm}^3$.

### Part 3: Ratio

$$\frac{(C/V)_{\text{MLC}}}{(C/V)_{\text{single}}} = \frac{d_{\text{single}}^2}{d_{\text{layer}}^2} = \left(\frac{3\text{ mm}}{0.05\text{ mm}}\right)^2 = 60^2 = 3600$$

The multilayer architecture achieves dramatically higher volumetric efficiency because capacitance scales as $1/d$ while volume scales as $d$, so shrinking the dielectric thickness (and stacking many thin layers) improves $C/V \propto 1/d^2$.

$$\boxed{(0.00197,\ 7.0832,\ 3600)}$$
